Directory

of

Popular Missions

PART I

THEORY

CHAPTER 1: ABOUT THE MISSION

Article 1: Name

1.The popular missions, or missions to the people, are known by many different names such as: Popular Missions; Missions to the town; Missions to the faithful; Holy Missions; “ad intra” Missions; Sacred Missions;1Traditional Missions; Missions to the Catholics; Missions to the interior or Internal Missions, etc.

Article 2: Nature

2It is a popular and simple form of preaching The Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ to the whole Town of God. It is the fulfillment of Christ’s missionary mandate: “Go into the whole world and proclaim the Gospel to every creature. Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved; whoever does not believe will be condemned (Mk 16:15-16).

The missionary prolongs Jesus Christ’s work who began to preach and to say: "Repent, because the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand" (Mt 4:17).

Article 3: Purpose

3The end of popular Missions follows the missionary mandate and is very well expressed by Saint Louis Marie Grignion de Montfort: "renewal of Christianity in believers”2; and by Saint Alphonsus Maria of Liguori: “the end of the missions (is) the conversion of sinners.”3 His Holiness John Paul II teaches that the popular Mission “is effective when…it impels to conversion, that is to say, the return to the truth and to God’s friendship of those who have lost their faith and grace because of sin; it calls routine Christians to a more perfect life, it gives fervor to souls, it convinces people to live the beatitudes, and it draws priestly and religious vocations.” 4

Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity

4The analogous principle of the missions is the missions ‘ad gentes.’ For all of them it is indispensable to be familiar with Pope John Paul II’s encyclical, “Redemptoris missio.”

5The missionary duty is “unique and identical in all parts of the world and in any circumstance, though it is not practised identically due to the fact that it depends on particular instances. The differences are not based on intrinsic reasons of the mission itself, but on the diverse situations in which it is developed.” 5

6Its ultimate principle is found in the “ad intra” Trinitarian processions and the “ad extra” missions. There are two “ad intra” processions: the generation of the Son and the expiration of the Holy Spirit. God is an intelligent being; the object of his understanding is his own essence: He understands himself. The concept that God eternally forms of himself is the Word. Between the Father and the Son they exhale the Holy Spirit through love.6

7The temporary missions, or “ad extra” missions, include the eternal processions and they add a new manner of presence:

- First, the sending of his Son, Supreme and Eternal Missionary: "God sent his Son" (Gal 4:4).

- Secondly, the sending of the Holy Ghost: “God sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts” (Gal 4:6).

8The temporary missions, or “ad extra” missions, can be visible or invisible.

There are two visible missions:

-The Incarnation, which is a substantial mission: “The Word became flesh...” (Jn 1:14);

-and the descent of the Holy Ghost at Pentecost, which is a representative mission: “then there appeared to them tongues as of fire, which parted and came to rest on each one of them” (Act 2:3).

9And throughout the history of the Church, the invisible, temporal mission is the Trinitarian indwelling of sanctifying grace in the soul of the faithful, because the three Persons come to dwell in the soul: In this we know that we remain in Him and He in us: “He has given us his Spirit” (Jn 4:13); “Whoever loves me will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him” (Jn 14:23).

The popular mission seeks to communicate to people the invisible “ad extra” mission: that the Trinity dwells within souls by grace.

10A principle that should govern the whole missionary activity of our Institute, because it is the revelation of the salvific will of God, is the rule that Saint Paul formulated to his disciple, Timothy, bishop and missionary: “God wants all men to be saved and to reach the full knowledge of the truth” (1Tim 2:4).

11Therefore, all those who truly love God know that He has not predestined anyone to eternal condemnation, and because of this, they make use of all ordinary and extraordinary means in order to reach every man’s salvation through Jesus Christ, the only Savior, and to be able to say together with Blessed Louis Orione: "Lord, place me at the mouth of hell, so I, through your mercy, may seal it.“ 7

12Conscious that “there is no salvation through anyone else, nor there is any other name under heaven given to the human race by which we are to be saved” (Act 4:12), the missionaries of the Institute understand, together with the Tradition and the perennial Magisterium, that “there is no salvation outside the Church,”8 because “the Church is the same Christ who lives among us...; it is the mysterious dwelling of Jesus Christ with us; it is another Christ,”9 and it is only in Jesus Christ, and under the action of the Holy Spirit, that men can enter into communion with God: “No one comes to the Father except through me” (Jn 14:6). As John Paul II expresses: “This unique and

universal mediation, far from being an obstacle on the walk towards God, is the way established by God Himself, and of which Christ has full consciousness."10

13There are diverse ways to belong to Christ's Church. In whichever manner, salvation comes only through Jesus Christ. Our mission is to make it so that all men be members of the Church “in act,” as it is clearly evident that salvation is offered to all men: "Christ died for all, and man's supreme vocation is only one, that is to say, divine. In consequence, we should believe that the Holy Spirit offers to all men the possibility, in a form only known to God, of being associated to this paschal mystery."11

Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions

14Our way of viewing the paradigm of all missions is that of the first mission of the disciples narrated by Saint Luke, chapter 10.

15... The Lord appointed 72 others... (v 1). God is the one who designates and chooses His missionaries. As He did before with the 72 disciples, He continues to do so now through His Church. Bishops and religious superiors choose missionaries in His name and with His authority.

16...and He sent them... (v 1). God not only chooses, but also sends. This sending resembles the sending of the Son : “As the Father has sent me, so I send you” (Jn 20:21). It is this sending which formally constitutes the mission.12

17… in pairs... (v 1). Our Lord had His reasons to act in this way and, in fact, many people continue proceeding in the same way. Saint Gregory the Great said: "He sent them in this way because there are two precepts of charity: love of God and love of neighbor; and there cannot be charity with less than two: this shows that whoever has no charity with his brothers, should not take the responsibility of preacher." 13 Our Constitutions say: "it is a fact that in mathematics one plus one is two, but one man plus another man are two thousand men. A man together with another grows in courage and strength, fear disappears, and he can escape from any trap." 14

18...ahead of him... (v 1). Christ sends His missionaries so that they would prepare the road by which He Himself would come to souls. This is the great consolation of the authentic missionary, the certainty of being sent by Whom and for Whom it is that comes to men. The missionary is a precursor, like Saint John the Baptist, who proclaims with his words and actions: "... A Man is coming after me" (Jn 1:30). From this comes the unyielding confidence in the inexhaustible power of the mission to bring about the conversion of men. It is Jesus Christ Himself who wants to come to them.

19... to every town and place... (v 1). There is no place where a soul is that is prohibited to the missionary. The missionary should go to the most humble houses, to the highest of high places, to the most rugged and rough places, where there are less people, where they expect less fruits, where the people are most unruly, where there are the most difficulties...there, the missionary should go taking his own staff, by automobile, plane, on foot or horse, sulky or ship...because this is his vocation, and to this obedience sends him.

20... where He intended to go (v 1). We are His ambassadors: We are, then, ambassadors of Christ, as if God appealed through us (2 Cor 5:20). Our mission is to bring Christ: "There is no true evangelization, if the name, the doctrine, the life, the promises, the Kingdom, the mystery of Jesus of Nazareth, Son of God are not announced." 15

21...And He said to them: “The harvest is abundant but the laborers are few; so, ask the master of the harvest to send out laborers for his harvest" (v 2). The apostolic work is enormous; we have to cover our ears when someone contradicts the words of the Lord, saying that there are many vocations. The laborers will always be few and the harvest will always be abundant. Only “thieves and robbers,”16 only a “mercenary”17 pastor can be so criminal as deflecting, discouraging, not working for, or being against vocations, because he does the work of a thief who comes to steal, to kill and to destroy... who leaves the sheep and runs away."18 It is always necessary to pray to God asking for workers for His harvest; and one of the great fruits of the popular Missions is vocations to consecrated life.

22Go on your way, behold, I am sending you like lambs among wolves (v 3). Our Lord insists: Go..., alerting us of the dangers that we will face. We are defenseless prophets, we only have spiritual weapons: Put on the armor of God so that you may be able to stand firm against the tactics of the devil. For our struggle is not with flesh and blood but with the principalities, with the powers, with the world rulers of this present darkness, with the evil spirits in the heavens. Therefore, put on the armor of God, that you may be able to resist on the evil day and, having done everything, to hold on your ground. So stand fast with your loins girded in truth, clothed with righteousness as a breastplate, and your feet shod in readiness for the gospel of peace. In all circumstances, hold faith as a shield, to quench all the flaming arrows of the evil one. And take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the spirit, which is the word of God. With all prayer and supplication, pray at every opportunity in the Spirit. To that end, be watchful with all perseverance and supplication for all the holy ones ...(Eph 6:11-18). Pastoral work means the cross, difficulties, dangers, sufferings: it means not taking advantage of the milk, meat, or the wool of the sheep, it is necessary to be like Saint Paul: I want not what is yours but you (2 Cor 12:14). Those who evacuate the cross, evacuate the pastoral work. That is why there are so many strident and clamorous pastoral failures. The sheep will not follow a stranger; they will run away from him, because they do not recognize the voice of strangers (Jn 10:5).

23Do carry neither a bag, nor a sack, nor sandals (v 4). It does not mean that our Lord wishes us to lack all goods, but it refers to the spirit of poverty that every missionary should have. They should not be attached to unnecessary things. The complete concern should be for no other than the missionary end. It is necessary to trust limitlessly in Providence, using all means.

24And do not greet anyone along your way (v 4). The task is urgent, there is no time to waste, nor occasions to do good: "the occasion is like iron, it is necessary to strike while its hot." The charity of Christ impels us (2 Cor 5:14).

25Into whatever house you enter, first say: " Peace to this house" (v 5). It is necessary to go where people live, to their environment, where they work. Nowadays, asking people to come to the Temple is not enough. It is necessary to go and meet the people! The first sermon of the Mission is usually about peace,19 because the peace of Christ is the purpose of the popular mission. The great work of the popular Mission is the pacification of souls in order to reconcile them with God.

26If a peaceful person lives there, your peace will rest on him (v 6). Peace is the greeting, the program and the fruit of the popular Missions. That is why personal visits are so important, they aim to place all people into the grace of God, and that is to carry peace. For that reason, it is necessary to guide people's conversation, to avoid being wrapped up in their topics, but pointing to their conversion. If not, (peace) will return to you (v 6). Peace which comes from God can not be without effect, if it does not rest on those visited, it will return to the missionaries who will benefit from it. Those missionaries who wish other people’s peace win merits for themselves.

27Stay in the same house...( v 7). The apostolic visit should not be a “medical visit.” It is necessary to take enough time to be able to detect the spiritual necessities of the family, their difficulties, to be able to carry out a consultation, to answer their doubts, to break their sophisms contrary to the faith, etc.

It is not advisable to accept, during the Mission, invitations to eat at family houses, because lunches are usually prolonged too much, and this provokes detriment of the Mission, since the necessary hour to rest and the contact with the other missionaries would be left aside. It is preferable that the families, in an organized manner, bring food to where all of the missionaries meet. In a very exceptional situation, it could be acceptable to eat with the families, but after-meal chats must be avoided. We should be disposed to everything, accommodate ourselves to the customs, as the Word surrendered,20 however, we should not consent to sin.

28...Because the laborer deserves his salary...Whatever town you enter and they welcome you, eat what is offered to you (v 7). You should not reject the alms that they freely offer, moreover, it allows them to make a charitable act, and to help to finance the expenses of the mission. According to our experience each mission is paid by itself. To reject charity could be seen as a neglect and it is necessary to educate for charity. 21

29Do not move from house to house (v 7). That is to say, in a hurry, as doing a census, but giving more importance to the spiritual fruits of each visit than to the quantity of houses you visit.

30...Cure the sick in it …(in the city)... (v 9). The physical and material attention of the sick is convenient, but one should not lose sight of the purpose of the visit, transforming it into a social visit.

31...And say to them: "The Kingdom of God is at hand for you" (v 9). The expression “Kingdom of God” appears 50 times in the Gospels; " Reign of Heavens ” 39 times, it has three meanings:

a) It has been prepared with the work of the patriarchs and prophets in the Old Testament and it became present in the Person and work of Christ. 22

b) It descends in Pentecost thanks to the Holy Spirit of whom the Catholic Church will be born. It is the earthly phase of the Kingdom, which is universal, spiritual, internal and external (that is to say, social with its sacraments and hierarchy), which does not exclude the bad and their mixture with the good, which has to be discovered, conquered and expanded.

c) It comes on the day of the Final Judgment, time only known by God and which will take us by surprise (Mk 13:32). It is the celestial phase of the Kingdom.

In the mission, the Kingdom of God is spoken of in its second meaning: the Church whose Head is Christ, as an external Universal Kingdom (members, temples), and internal (the Grace). This Kingdom should be extended. It is necessary to conquer souls for this Kingdom, and in this way to expand it.

The popular mission is a pure mission and typically missionary, or rather, ordered for the salvation of souls. It is focused on the metanoia, that they will repent (Mk 6:12), on the renewal, on the change of “modes of thinking.”

32Whatever town you enter and they do not receive you, go out into the streets and say: " The dust of your town that clings to our feet, even that, we shake off against you.” Yet know this: the Kingdom of God is at hand" (v 10,11). The act of shaking the dust in the place, city or house where it proceeds shows that it is profane earth in which one does not want to participate, and in that way, you it gives testimony against them (Mk 6:11). We are also taught, that even in the event of rejection, it is necessary to know how to announce, as far as possible, the Gospel.

33I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom on that day than for that town, woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! Because if the mighty Dees done in your midst had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would long ago have repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes. But it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgement than for you. And as for you, Capernaum, Will you be exalted to heaven? You will go down to the netherworld (v 12:15)! Even the Supreme and Eternal missionary knew the apparent missionary failure. If He knew it, we can also know it: No disciple is above his teacher, no slave is above his master (Mt 10:24). An apparent missionary failure should not disappoint us, on the contrary, it should revive our apostolic work.

34.Whoever listens to you, listens to me; whoever rejects you, rejects me. And whoever rejects me, rejects the one who sent me (v 16). For that reason, it is necessary to have much delicacy in order to avoid being the cause of the rejection. It is necessary to have great kindness of heart and to be clearly conscious that our words should be those of Christ. Who rejects the missionary, rejects Christ and rejects the Father. The good missionary should put into practice the advice that Saint John Marie Vianney gave to a priest who complained about the sterility of his apostolic efforts: "You have raised your prayers to God, cried, sighed, complained; but, have you fasted, kept vigil slept on the floor and whipped yourself ? While you have not done these, do not believe that you have tried your best.” 23

35The 72 returned rejoicing... (v 17). Inevitably, the missionary always returns from the mission with an immense happiness. Perhaps, there is no happier man than an authentic missionary, because: Blessed the one who comes in the name of God! (Sal 118:26). Promises made by God will be executed: "Blessed are the peacemakers ..." (Mt 5:9).

36...saying: "Lord, even the demons are subject to us because of your name.” He told them: “I have observed Satan fall like lightning from the sky" (v 17-18). That is the effect of a good mission well carried out: the fall of the demon for not being able to capture souls by sin. And that is the motive for the missionary’s happiness, although, there are motives more lofty.

37Behold, I have given to you the power to tread upon serpents and scorpions and upon the full force of the enemy and nothing will harm you... (v 19). For that reason, not even all of the forces of hell together will have power over the missionary, because to him does receives power from Christ. Nothing can harm the true disciple of the Lord: do not be afraid of those who kill the body, they can not kill the soul (Mt 10:28).

38...Nevertheless,” do not rejoice because the spirits are subject to you; but rejoice because your names are written in heaven” (v 20). The greatest motive for the missionary’s happiness is to have been chosen by God to preach his Gospel; election and mission which will not be left without recompense: My brothers, if anyone among you should stray from the truth and someone brings him back, he should know that whoever brings back a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins (Jas 5: 19-20).

39At that very moment He rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I give you praise, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, for although you have hidden these things from the wise and the learned you have revealed them to the childlike. Yes, Father, such has been your gracious will. All things have been handed over to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and who the Father is, except the Son and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal him" (v 21,22). Jesus showed himself inundated with joy, just as the missionary who has finished a Mission feels, because he that principally works during the mission is Jesus. He is always the first Missionary and the first one to be happy. Jesus is filled with our joy, and we should let him inundate us with His joy. These are hidden things to those who consider themselves wise and intelligent, but in fact, are arrogant. Such is the gracious will of the Father. Every Mission originates in the Trinity and terminates in the Trinity, in benefit to those to whom the Son wishes to reveal this.

40Turning to the disciples in private He said :”Blessed are the eyes that see what you see. For I say to you, many prophets and kings desired to see what you see, but did not see it, and to hear what you hear, but did not hear it” (v 23-24). Blessed by experiencing the reality of God’s Kingdom, which is established thanks to the Messiah, Jesus Christ, through whom the Father acts, a thing seen neither by the prophets who announced it - Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Daniel... - nor by the kings of whom the Messiah would descend: - David, Solomon... - but seen by the missionaries.

41The text of the Gospel according to Saint Luke finishes with two facts that, for us, manifest the two great foundations of the popular Missions: one is the charity and mercy that the missionary should have. Teacher, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”…"You shall love the Lord, your God, with all your heart, with all your being, with all your strength, and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself " . ... And “Who is my neighbor?" ...He said: "The one who treated him with mercy" (v 25,29,37).

42The other one is prayer. When there is no prayer, there is no charity; and when there is no charity, there is no prayer, and by reason of this lacking, there are not many authentic missionaries... you are anxious and worried about many things; and there is need of only one thing. Mary has chosen the best part and it will not be taken from her (v 41-42).

Article 6: Classes

43There are different classes of Popular Missions:

- The most common is the intensive one, which is carried out during ten, fifteen, or more days. In theory, this would be all the days necessary to dispose all to confess.

- The permanent one, which lasts most of the year, especially, the ministry of home visits.

- The youth mission, carried out together with the intensive one or, preferably, in the secondary schools, universities or in any other place of concentration of youth.

- The children’s mission, which is similar to the previous one but is focused on children.

- The mission for the sick, dedicated especially to them.

- The industrial mission, when it is carried out in the industries.

- The open Mission, when it is carried out through any media, especially, the television and the radio.

- The Mission, according to the territory, can be general, (organized in a dioceses), parochial or in buildings of many families, centers for listening to the Word or other variations which are discovered to be convenient.

44With much profit there can be, at the same time, different types of popular Missions according to the necessities and, mainly, according to the possibilities.

Article 7: Importance and Necessity

45God willed that the world be saved through missionaries. Throughout time, God sent workers to cultivate his vineyard. In the Old Testament, He sent the patriarchs and prophets; in the New Testament, the Supreme and Eternal Missionary: Jesus Christ, sent by his Father; then, the Apostles and their successors were sent: Go into the whole world and proclaim the Gospel to every creature (Mk 16:15). The whole history of the Church testifies the sending of laborers... that is why the wise father Contenson affirms: "Only through the missions do souls attain their eternal salvation." 24 For that reason, Saint Alphonsus says: "Clearly seen are the efforts of hell to avoid the missions." 25

The importance of preaching and the missions is so great that the Church points out that the priest has “among his main duties, the announcement of the Gospel of God to everybody." 26 And to the parish priests it prescribes that: "During certain times...the parish priests should organize those forms of preaching named spiritual exercises and sacred missions or others adapted to these necessities." 27

46Likewise, the Third General Latin-American Episcopal Conference in Puebla: “It would go in a simultaneous form to the groups and to the multitudes. For these last ones, the popular Missions have great effectiveness, conveniently renewed in an evangelizing line."28

47Convinced of the necessity of the “Missions to the People,” John Paul II repeats untiringly: “Because of this, today I repeat with greater force and conviction what I have already wrote in the Apostolic Letter “Catechesi Tradendae": "The traditional missions are irreplaceable for a periodic and vigorous renovation of Christian life. 29” 30

48The urgency of preaching has its foundation in Holy Scripture: "When writing to the Romans, Saint Paul highlights: faith is by preaching, by the Word of Christ (1 Co 1:30). Therefore, it is necessary to go, to speak, to preach, to teach, to announce, so that men could believe and invoke." 31

Article 8: The Popular Missions at Present

49There have always been people who “dream up vain pretexts to impede the mission in their parishes." 32 Among them, there are those who affirm that they are not appropriate for our days; that is why John Paul II must remember their perennial presence: "I manifest to you, moreover, my gratitude and that of the whole Church because of the interest and the good will in maintaining and modernizing the fervor and effective practice of the popular Missions. Remembering what the Divine Teacher commanded: Go and teach to all people..., teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you (Mt 28:19-20), we can do no less than obey with courage and with joy, announcing to all men that Jesus Christ has come to be for us, on the part of God, wisdom as well as justice, sanctification and redemption (1 Co 1:30).33

50“Christ's command and the Apostle's severe warning 34 are still valid. They have been the stimulus which has made the great Fathers intrepid and untiring, the great Saints, to whom it is necessary to make reference constantly if we really want to illuminate and to save our brothers: Ignatious of Loyola, Phelip Neri, Vicent of Paul, Alphonsus Marie of Liguori, Saint Paul of the Cross, Louis Grignion of Monfort, Gaspar of Buffalo, Francis de Sales, John Baptist Vianney, Maximilian Kolbe: brilliant and concrete men who ‘Popular Missions’ of maximum value." 35

Article 9: The Present Time:

Renovated Methods and Modernized Criteria

51All missionary saints have known how to adapt to the times and diverse necessities of their audience,36 as Saint Alphonsus M. of Liguori expressly states: "What use is there for the sick to report prescriptions which the doctor has prescribed at random, before knowing their illnesses?”37

52In our days John Paul II insists: "...I exhort all of you to renew them, to revalue them, to propose them again with modernized methods and criteria adapted to the dioceses and to the parishes, in accordance with the local Churches.” 38

53"Today, for an effective work in the area of preaching, it is necessary, before all else, to know very well the spiritual and psychological reality of the Christians who live in the modern society. It is necessary to admit, realistically, and with deep and tormented sensibility that Christians today, for the most part, feel misplaced, confused, perplexed and even disappointed; they have spread before them ideas contrasting the real truth which has been revealed and always taught; ideas that are truly and properly heresies in the dogmatic and moral sphere have been spread, creating doubts, confusions, rebellions, the liturgy has even been manipulated; they are immersed in an intellectual and moral "relativism," and due to this, in permissive-ism, Christians are tempted by atheism, agnosticism, the vaguely moralistic illuminism, by a sociological Christianity, without defined dogmas and without an objective morality. It is necessary to know the man of today in order to be able to understand how to listen to him and to love him as he is, not to excuse the wrong, but to discover his roots, well-convinced that everybody can have salvation and mercy under, the condition of not rejecting them consciously and obstinately.”

54“Today, the evangelical figures of the good Samaritan, the father of the prodigal son, the Good Shepherd prove to be particularly present. It is necessary to constantly take the pulse of our time, to be able to know the current man.”

55The Pope’s words are very clear if some elements are taken into account:

To illuminate minds and

To encourage maternally.

56“For an authentic and effective ‘mission,’ it is necessary to illuminate minds in a complete and sure way. Today, it is not enough to state a concept, it is necessary to listen first, to realize where the other is, in his path of searching or in his drama of defeat or escape, it is necessary to explain things and to be attentive to the other’s demands.”

57To encourage maternally: “Today, it is necessary to be patient and to begin again from the beginning, from the “preambles of the faith” up to the “novisimos,” with clear, documented and satisfactory exposition. It is necessary to form the intelligence with illuminated and strong convictions, because it is the only way to form consciences. Today, above all it is necessary to capture and to inculcate the “sense of mystery,” the necessity of humility of reason when facing the Infinite and the Absolute, the logic of confidence and trust in Christ and the Church, which is loved and founded by Him to always give men the peace of truth and the happiness of grace. It is a delicate and even tiring task which demands careful preparation and psychological sensibility; however, it is absolutely necessary.” 39

58Not only that but also “…it is necessary to encourage people maternally with the same love as Christ. The “popular Mission” is effective when, accompanied by prayer and penance, it impels to conversion, that is to say, the return to the truth and friendship of God for those who had lost their faith and grace because of sin, it calls routine Christians to a more perfect life, it gives fervor to souls, it convinces people to live the beatitudes, and it raises priestly and religious vocations. To achieve these effects, firm doctrine is required, but overall, kindness of heart! So, clothe yourselves with the same sentiments of Jesus and proclaim to everybody what the author of the letter to the Hebrews wrote: Let us confidently approach the throne of grace to receive mercy and to find grace for timely help (Heb 4:16).

Article 10: Useful Means

59In ages past, the missions revolved around two main elements: the sermons and confessions. Nowadays another is added: the visit to families.

The Sermons

60The missionary’s sermons are useful yet when the pastor preaches every Sunday, in a way that even the more ignorant people could get fruits, since he is not speaking about things pertaining to them, or about the problems that his parishioners present to him, “by force of always hearing the same voice, one ends up not being impressed with what hears.”40

61One of the reasons for the massive attendance to the missions is that new voices, which speak simply and popularly, are heard, together with the explication of the eternal truths which are more effective for moving hearts, such as the importance of eternal salvation, the malice of sin, death, judgment, hell, eternity…,etc.

The Confessions

62They are not few who, after having spent many years without confessing or after making a bad confession, finally during the Mission make a confession with a good disposition. It is the main fruit of the Missions. Many sacrilegious confessions, which are made keeping their sins in silent because of shame, are remedied. Now, they know that there are many foreign priests whom they do not know and who soon will be gone, people decide to vomit all their sins, which they had kept in secret for a long time.

63For that reason the Mission should last the enough time in each place so that all the parishioners could have their confessions heard by the missionaries.

The Home Visits

64Nowadays, it does not suffice to call the sheepfold, but it is necessary to go and look for the sheep. Each missionary is able to say, as John Paul II did when he visited the Saint Francis Roman church in Rome: “Today, I come to your church [to your house] to carry out the principle apostolic ministry: the ministry of the visit.”41

65Each family from our parishes should remember: Do not reject Christ who passes by in the person of the missionary! Saint Alphonsus affirms: “I am certain that for those who have gone to the sermons of the mission, if one dies within the year, with difficulty would he be condemned.”42

Article 11: Objections Against Popular Missions

66Saint Alphonsus refutes the main objections. In the first place: “...that the fruit of the missions turns into smoke, which seems great but, however, is of short duration, since, after the mission, sinners behave worse than before.” I answer: I hope all those who are converted persevere until death! Human misery makes many sinners lose the grace that they had recovered. But, even if there were no other advantages, it is certain that bad customs and scandals disappear during the mission, blasphemies cease, much restitution is made, and many bad confessions are repaired. Moreover, it is not true that all sinners behave worse after the mission than before; many of them persevere in God’s grace, and if some of them relapse, they are conserved far from mortal sin during many months; at least, due to the sermons heard in the mission, they acquire greater knowledge of God and of the importance of salvation, and a greater horror of sin, so that luckily, if they relapse, they will rise again before the paschal fulfillment. I am certain that for those who have gone to the sermons of the mission, if one dies within a year, with difficulty would he be condemned. The fruit of the Mission can be seen to last for at least one or two years after it, and if it doesn’t, it would be the fault of the priests of the place that do not make an effort to conserve the fruit of the mission with instructions, taking care to meet with the people to make a meditation and a visit to the Blessed Sacrament, and overall, being faithful to confessions. Sometimes, a year after the Mission, there are few fruits, but why? Because of the negligence of the priests who do not want to be bothered.”

67In the second place: “ …the parish priest says missions disturb consciences due to the numerous scruples caused by the sermons…Would this priest want sinners to sleep in the lethargy of vice, in the bosom of that damned peace, which is the stamp of their condemnation? Would that the consciences be disturbed! What the devil wants is that the false peace of his unfortunate slaves, who live in a state of perdition, be not disturbed.”

68In the third place: “… that the mission events finish at night, so it gives cause for many scandals. I answer that full fantasy is needed to claim that many sins are committed during the mission because it is preached at night. Precisely then do all the inhabitants feel sacred fear, and moreover, those who go to the mission, and at least during this time, would not interfere by tempting the others, because they know very well that they could not find accomplices. But, supposing the case that there was a libertine man who would dare to tempt a girl, would the events of the mission have to be omitted just because they finish at night? It is said that one should not do wrong so that good would come; holy and good; but it is one thing to do wrong and another to allow it. If it were necessary to omit all good things to avoid all possible danger of evil things, we would have to prohibit all the saints’ feasts, processions, pilgrimages to shrines, because some disorder will always emanate from them; in the same way, we would have to prohibit confessions, communions, attendance at Mass, because there are also scandals and sacrileges from them. It is known that the Church not only permits these things, but she approves and imposes them. But, our contradictor replies: as it is preached at night, so it results that the mission is the cause of these sins. I respond in turn: would they stop committing sins without the mission? If the mission were not preached, bad habits, fights, blasphemies and all the existent scandals would continue, but if it is preached, thousands of sins would be avoided at least while it lasts.”

69In the fourth place: “certain missionaries speak imprudently from the pulpit about sins heard in confession, which contributes to people conceiving an aversion for the confessional, and, for fear of being humiliated in public, they omit confessing their sins. I am amazed that the afore-mentioned pastor repeats what people of bad conscience, who dislike the mission, allege. When missionaries arrive at any place, the first thing they do is to become informed by the most prudent men about the sins that reign above all in the population. so that the morality of the sermons could frequently deal with them, and they take much care not to speak about certain particular acts that could have a special relation with what they had heard in confession. Therefore, with what will they occupy themselves from the pulpit? Perhaps ecstasy, raptures, visions or revelations? The most common sins which are ordinarily committed by habit everywhere, such as impure acts, blasphemy, hate, theft, and other similar ones will be treated and spoken about.”

70In the fifth place: “he [the pastor] has not requested the mission because to request it gives rise to the people suspecting that the pastor does not carry out his duty since he is asking for outside help. It can be said that this difficulty, or better said, this excuse, is mixed with his pride. I think entirely the contrary: there is not the least dishonor in the parish priest requesting the mission, but there is dishonor in not requesting it, because omitting the care to request the mission in his parish gives rise to thinking that the he is afraid that his own faults will be discovered. On the other hand, when the pastor fulfills his obligation well, the missionaries will praise his behavior not only in the town, but also before the bishop."

71In the sixth place: “his parish had a mission three years ago and scarce fruits are reported from missions when they are frequent, because the people become accustomed to them, so that they do not make an impression: I answer that, regularly, the mission should not be repeated after a short period of time in the same place, but that three years is not a short period of time; ordinarily, after that interval, many have forgotten the sermons, many are those who have also relapsed and many more are those who have become cold, and with a new mission, some of them will revive their fervor and others will raise themselves up from their fall. Apart from that, it is not true that the repetition of missions ceases to produce fruits; when the mission is repeated in the same place, even when that lively compunction is not noticed that was noticed in the first one, all the same, the fruit which the town can take from it will not fail to be great, because, as I already mentioned, many sinners rise from their relapses, many cold souls revive their fervor, and many, at least, reaffirm with steadiness the good way.“ 43

72Another objection against popular Missions that is widespread is the economic cost. According to our experience, the Missions pay for themselves. An economic problem does not exist if the popular Mission is done well. God will not be outdone in generosity! He it is who said: Mine is the silver, mine is the gold, says the Lord (Ag 2:9 ).

CHAPTER 2: HISTORY OF THE POPULAR MISSIONS

Article 1: Pre-history of the Popular Missions

73We can talk about a so-called “pre-history” of popular missions, if we keep in mind the contributions inherited from the magisterial experience of the Church that has contributed to its systematization.

74In the beginning, what stands out as an exemplary model of all popular missions is the missionary action of the Prophets and the Apostles, which, over and above the ordinary ministry carried out in order to maintain faith and grace, stood out in an extraordinary mission that had as its goal winning souls for Christ. In the book of Acts, elements which will systematize the Popular Missions can be corroborated.

75Subsequently, the epoch of persecutions and of the first heresies produced great preachers who - with the strength of their words and even with the signature of their miracles - won souls for Christ in special missions, which in their kind will continue to solidify the popular missions. This preaching was the best means to confront heresies, which consisted in instructing the faithful who many times found themselves abandoned by their shepherds.

76Some examples of these are the missions carried out by Saints Ireneus of Lyon, Cyprian, Gregory Thaumaturgy, Gregory Nazianzen, Anthony Abbot, Pacomio, Columba, Eusebius of Vercelli, Hilario of Poitiers; especially those who “while passing through town” preached about the end times, mercy, and Christian customs.

77During the Middle Ages, we find an important phase for the systematization in the preaching especially motivated by the promulgations of the crusades. Each crusade was preceded by the preaching of great orators, such as Peter the Hermit or Saint Bernard, and these masters of the Word did not work according to a determined plan, but, obliged by the circumstances of the moment, carried out for this occasion a kind of popular mission for the crusaders as for the town. In this way, it was possible to awaken the spirit of Christian penance and a holy enthusiasm for the Holy Land in the society, a powerful impulse that animated Christendom throughout the centuries.

78It is in the XII century when popular missions began to appear, highlighting the figures of Saint Bernard - preacher of the Crusade and renowned refuter of the heresies of his time - and Saint Robert - who insisted in penance and in the vanity of worldly things. The themes are always constant: penance, conversion, novisimos, mercy...

79The missions begin to be more frequent until they are transformed into a very effective element for the conversion of the people, moving them to confession, to charity to pay for the crusades, to acts of charity, and to constancy in receiving the other sacraments.

80After the XI and XII centuries, reacting against the relaxation of the priests in the active life, the canons regular arose, secular priests who united themselves to take on a life in common according to the rule of Saint Augustine. With this goal, in 1120 Saint Norbert founded the Premonstratensians, fully dedicated to apostolic preaching.

81Nevertheless, before the XIII century, with the exception of the great shepherds of souls, the people were driven away by preaching that was, at best, theological dispute.

82The necessity to expose in a simple form the essence of the true faith grew with the appearance of the heresies of the “cataros and valdenses.” As a result, the mendicant orders arose as an authentic reformation that, through the testimony of evangelical poverty and preaching outside of the parochial environment, achieved great successes in their missions.

83The fourth Lateran Council (1215), gave stability to the type of life offered by mendicant orders.

84By then, the Franciscan preachers had in mind the advice of Honorio III, when, in 1223, he wrote to them to confirm their Order: "would that your elocution be purified and corrected for the utility and edification of the people, announcing to your listeners vices and virtues, sorrows and glories, the sermon with brevity because it is an abridged word that our Lord has made over the earth."

85.The Dominicans, according to the purpose of their order, and approved in 1216, forged prepared preachers with a firm theology in order to defend the faith from the attacks of heretics.

86To make a principle task of the ministry of the word of God, and the reason for being from a religious society, were completely new things in the Church. From the beginning, this idea was revealed as very fertile.

87In the new dedication that these orders conceded to preaching, behind the figure of Saint Francis and Saint Dominic shined that of Saint Anthony of Padua (X 1231), and of Berthold of Ratisbona (X 1272).

88During this period it is admired how public activities ceased when the missionaries passed. An author from that epoch relates: "all, the young and the old with banners at front, went to the city to listen to the sermon and to sing the praises of God. They preached morning, noon, and night...The Way of the Cross was made in Churches and squares..."

89Here, the pious theater, solemn entrances, processions of penitents, and representations of the Passion are joined as resources for preaching.

90When Boniface VIII instituted the Holy Year for the jubilee of 1300, the special preaching of indulgences prevailed in the pulpits with the thematic logic of the reform of customs.

Some years later the three immediate forerunners of the Popular Missions arose:

91*Saint Vincent Ferrer (1419): he consecrated himself as prototype of Popular Missions in France, Spain and Italy. He preached about sin, death, hell, and especially about the universal judgment, which he considered to be near. He celebrated Mass and heard confessions early, and at night, he organized processions for penitents and flagellants.

92*Saint Bernardine of Siena (1444): disciple of Saint Vincent, he also used external elements and ceremonies, for example: bonfires of worldly things, the reconciliation of enemies...Many of those who came later imitated his method and repeated the written sermons he left.

93*Saint John of Capistrano (1456): he inherited Saint Bernardine's style. The “sermo ad status” arose during these years, pointing to the execution of the duty of the particular state.

94The preaching in general was very simple and moving, adapted to the public, and for this reason efficacious. They usually worried about recording forever in memory the truths of faith which had been preached by using songs, it was the spirit of the alive emotion of the end of the Middle Ages.

Article 2: The Popular Mission Properly Speaking

95The XVI century opened with the Protestant reformation, which was the culmination of an anticlerical ferment. But the same Counter reformation, at

the moment of the Council of Trent, gathered the desires for fervent renewal inside the Church in a great number of souls. The Popular Mission came about as a fruit of the missionary experience of the Church throughout the centuries.

96The triumph of the Catholic reformation (1545-1563), was mainly due to the work of the popular missions. It was necessary to reform the customs of the clergy first, for which new congregations of clergy regulars were particularly consecrated:

97The “Teatinos,” founded by Saint Cajetan of Thiene, aimed at the reform o f the clergy, but were also adapted to preaching.

98The Barnabites, founded by Saint Anthony Mary Zachariah, exhorted people to penance and the sacraments, for which they carried a big cross on their habits and they preached with a rope tied around their necks.

99The Jesuits, who in the missions utilized all possible means, by mandate from Saint Ignatius who, from the beginning, considered the popular mission as one of the best means for the apostolate of his Society.

100Saint Ignatious poured fourth many instructions in his “Rules for those who live in missions"; he insisted on the formation of the missionaries, he asked that they give talks and sermons during the missions, that they give catechism to children and adults, and that they administer the sacraments.

101Moreover, in 1590, Father Acquaviva, Superior General of the Society, gave very profitable norms: to discover the more common sins and vices of the town visited; to use many examples; to make solemn and lively processions; to go two by two; a minimum of eight missionaries in each center; to speak about the peace of God and the means to reach it in the initial speech; to use the influence of teachers and authorities; to converse personally with people during free times; to pin point the places where more profit could be obtained; to extend what is necessary to prepare consciences for confession; each priest should do a mission at least once a year; to renew baptismal promises, to concede indulgences at the end of the mission; to do controversies, because one learns by repetition, etc.

102The Oblates of Saint Ambrose, analogous to the Jesuits, were founded in 1578, by Saint Charles Borromeo; they are those who give the specific name of “mission” to this form of evangelization. They required a total disposition for the mission: "To carry out any ecclesiastical mission in any Church..." Saint Charles Borrromeo indicated the characteristics of missionary preaching: "You will use any means to touch your listeners, that they cry for their sins and repent; try to separate them from their vices and from their crimes, frightening them with the sight of the tortures of the eternal fire; to recommend them to the recompense of the life in heaven, informing them about zeal by means of the virtues and above all by the love of God and neighbor.”

103The Capuchins, founded in 1528 by Bernardino D`Asti, were characterized by their simple and popular preaching.

104.The popular mission, as we know it today, was born during the time of the Catholic Counter-reformation, by the work of the regular canons and clergymen. They aimed at reinforcing the faith of the people, reforming the customs, banishing heresies... For this reason, they preached over all of the ultimate end of man, penance and the sacraments. They especially stressed general confessions and the solemn renewal of the promises of Baptism at the end of the mission. Their duration oscillated between some days and some months, according to the circumstances. With Trent, the preaching of Catechism was given the first place among the ministries.

Article 3: Systematization of Popular Missions

105After the Protestant heresy, popular missions were aquiring a more serene and systematic character: to combat heresy and to confirm the religious and moral life of the Catholics. But in other countries, the popular mission has developed quickly until it becomes a specific institution consecrated to the extraordinary ministry and provided with an own character and structure.

a) In Spain: for example, Father Jerónimo López (1658), introduced some variations such as the penitential procession through the city with sermons along the way, preaching with a skull in hand and a “dialogue” with it, the act of contrition or “feeling of night," the solemn communion of the whole town, etc.

106b) In Italy: Father Landini, S. J., asked that, upon arrival to a city, the missionaries make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament, give vigorous sermons and discipline to men..." the discipline is,” he used to say, “in some manner, the practical confirmation of what is speculatively taught in the sermons." He was concerned that the Blessed Sacrament be exposed and devotion to the Passion be spread. He focused on immediate conversion. “The mission should not last more than ten days, in order that fervor not be lost, but after, the missionaries can stay to preach a retreat to priests, and to see those who were not able to attend...."

107Father Segneri, S.J (1694), used to begin the missions on Monday and finished them Sunday. The Mission included sermons, catechesis, penitential processions and a general communion. The topics were: the value of the soul, malice of the sin, death, eternity, the Sacraments, etc. At the end, people were vehemently urged to persevere in good. This priest was the one who systematized the method among the Jesuits.

108Cardinal Caraffa (1633), who later would be Paul IV, founded the congregation of the “Pii Operarii” in 1601: secular priests who lived in community to preach missions to towns and villages with the principal end of “teaching to all the way to salvation." Their missions lasted 10 days, because “he who does not allow himself to be affected in that time will never allow himself to be affected.” He Insisted on walking the streets inviting people, and the procession culminated with a great sermon in the afternoon.

109Saint Alphonsus Marie of Liguori founded the Congregation of the Holy Redeemer (Redemptorists) in 1732, with the purpose of giving missions, obliging themselves to it by simple vows. He insisted on some topics that he considered to be principle ones: mortal sin, death-judgement-hell, the Passion of Our Lord Jesus Christ, confession, trust in Mary, prayer. He also put as optional topics: mercy, God’s calls, the vanity of things, perseverance.

110Saint Leonard of Porto Maurizio OFM (1751), “the celestial patron of popular missions," according to Pius XI, in 1923, combined action and contemplation perfectly: "mission being always busy for God, solitude being always busy in God.” He abandoned his monastery to dedicate himself to the “campaign against the devil,” as he called the missions. He placed a good confession as the principle end of the missions. The first day, he placed the crucifix in a very visible place and said: "Here is a summary of what we will preach to you in these holy days: Jesus Crucified. “ In the morning, he gave instruction that lasted one hour; exposition of a relic of the Virgin with a few words about the Mother of God and finally a blessing given with the relic ended this exercise. In the afternoon, he gathered the town in procession singing songs of the mission; after came the exposition of the Holy Sacrament, a colloquy with the Eucharistic Christ and benediction. Then, the saint gave the great sermon of the afternoon; everything lasted about two hours. During the course of the mission two penitential processions were made; communion was distributed on several days... "I want to die on mission, with the sword in my hand against hell,” he said, and so it happened.

111c). In France: Saint Vincent de Paul (1581-1660), founded the “Congregation of the Mission,” or “Lazaristas,” to be devoted to the missions among peasants and to the formation of the clergy. He gave great importance to the teaching of catechism; he used to say: "The whole world will agree with the fact that the fruit taken from the mission comes through the catechism.” He established a day so that the missionaries could rest. In thirty years the Lazaristas gave more than 1,000 missions in France.

112Other important missionaries were: Father Le Nobletz, who took advantage of songs and drawings; Father Maunoir, S.J., whose missions were like the outline of the Exercises of Saint Ignatius. Father Condren; Monsignor Olier, founder of Saint Sulpicio; Saint John Eudes, founder of the Apostolic Missionaries of Jesus and Mary, who proposed much more duration to ensure the fruits of the mission: two months or more.

113Saint Louis Marie Grignion of Monfort founded, in 1705, the Missionary Fathers of the Company of Mary, characterized by their Marian devotion and their apostolic zeal. Saint Louis Marie always carried a cross and a statuette of the Virgin which he accommodated at Mass, in the confession box, in his room, etc. He especially used processions and songs. He also returned after a time to ensure the fruits; after the mission, his “return to the mission” lasted one week.

114The French Revolution with its wars extinguished the popular missions; but the storm ended and they began their rebirth.

115New congregations and great missionaries were born like: Monsignor Mazenod and the Oblates of Mary Immaculate, Saint Gaspar of Buffalo, Saint Vicent Palotti, and many others.

116d) In America: some figures are highlighted among others: Saint Francis Solano, Saint Toribio of Mogrovejo, Saint Roque Gonzalez, and a multitude of Jesuits, Franciscans, Mercedaries, etc

117During the XIX century, “Propaganda Fidei” is founded, and later on Pontifical Missionary Works. During this century Saint Thérèse is named as patron of the missions, and with that purpose, Pope Pius XI publishes an important document about the theme. The figures of Saint Anthony Marie Claret (1870), and Charles of Foucauld (1916), are highlighted.

118The universal Patrons of the missions are: Saint Francis Xavier (1506-1552), and Saint Thérèse of the Child Jesus (1873-1897). The Patron of Popular Missions is Saint Leonard de Porto Maurizio.

PART II

PRAXIS

119The praxis of the Popular Mission is very varied and rich, and depends for the most part on the missionary's charisma. But, without getting bogged down on minor details, we consider that it has three well-marked phases, they are: 1st the Pre - mission, 2nd the Mission itself; and 3rd the Post-mission.

Article 1: The Pre-mission

120The Pre-mission is of capital importance due to the best organization of the Mission, since beginning a Mission with everything ready is to possess, already at the beginning, the success of the whole Mission, because this is to ensure its fruits. On the contrary, not preparing the Mission is to tempt God. The collaboration of the pastor is fundamental for this preparation.

121This preparation certainly has its requirements, such as:

- To determine the area for the mission, the date, the plane of the area and to have maps for all of the missionaries, defining the zone of each one. To keep in mind celebrations which are characteristic of the area, and also the climate. In the plan, to divide into zones, to mark the routes for the processions; with that, to calculate the number of the faithful; the possible places to begin the procession before the missionary act.

122To know the area. To determine social structures, the religious situation, (attendance at Mass, vices, etc.), the pastoral attention and social problems that condition the religious life (work in a factory), etc.

123To advertise. For example, to make contests for Mission advertisement, of its slogan, its hymn and logo. The Mission should be announced, it should awaken interest, it should be favorably welcomed and interpreted well.

124To have campaigns for prayer and penance. To have a list of all the missionaries and of the lay people who help them; to organize adoration of the Most Holy Sacrament, the Holy Rosary; to request prayers from contemplatives and the sick, etc.

125Economy. To organize the expenses to pay for the food for the missionaries, images, rosaries, catechisms, song books, catechetical pamphlets, missals, Gospels, etc.

126Acceptance. To have the catholic spirit, that is to say, to accept the solidarity of other preachers and missionaries.

127The search for militants. To look for people to help in some aspect of the Mission: it is a way to seek their conversion, making them useful for the missionaries (for example: to look for chauffeurs, cooks, missionaries' companions, people in charge of publicity and propaganda, people who look for donations, people in charge of the sound system, etc.).

128Appointment of commissions. To divide the work: liturgy, catechism, entertainment, the children's Mission, the Mission to the sick, extraordinary ministers of the Eucharist, liturgical and popular choir, etc.

129Planning. To fix objectives, to choose blocks, to study the content of what is going to be transmitted, to determine the centers of the mission and to be familiar with them before the Mission, to determine special centers: for children (schools), for young people (clubs). To organize collective acts (processions). To form the group of lay and consecrated missionaries.

Article 2: The Mission Itself

130The Mission itself consists in three principle elements, they are:

- The visits to families

- The schedule of every day of the Mission and

- The missionary act of every day.

a. The Home Visits

131In the first place, the home visits should be primary. This centrifugal action, from the center to the periphery, is the search for the “lost sheep" (Lk 15:6). It is through the home visits that the spiritual situation of each of the faithful is known, in order to be able to do pre-sacrament catechesis, if it were necessary, in their homes. It is necessary to attend preferentially to the adults.

b. The Program of the Whole Mission

132At the same time, such an expansion of the missionaries seeks to develop a centripetal action, from the periphery to the center, because bringing people to the missionary center is the objective of, where the following should take place:

- The opening acts with the missionary mandate;

- The missionary acts of every day;

- The closing acts;

- The special acts during each day of the mission.

133For example, during the Eucharistic day, the bells should be rung every half hour, in order to remember that that day the Sacramental Jesus is being adored in the Church, and it brings the people to participation from their homes through ejaculatory prayers and acts of adoration. At night the Most Holy Sacrament is carried in procession, like in “Corpus." It produces many spiritual fruits and is very much appreciated by the people.

134Likewise, one day should be dedicated to the Virgin, that day can be a Saturday, adorning her image with flowers, and also organizing a continuous Rosary at the Church with shifts of thirty minutes to pray it in the church, for example.

135One day should be dedicated to the deceased, it is convenient to do it twice, at the beginning of the mission, to attract the people, and another at the end, with a visit and prayer for the dead in the cemetery, if possible.

136One day can be dedicated to the families, with the blessing of future mothers, marriages, homes, etc., where the Gospel of the family can be preached; and other days can be devoted to children, to youth, to workers, where there can be preaching about the Gospel of work, etc.

137There should also be a penitential day, in which confessions are heard for the whole day. Strictly speaking, it is ideal that a missionary Priest stay always in the missionary center and that people know that he is at their disposal from the first day of the Mission.

138These special dedications for each day have as objective to concentrate on each type of person in particular, and to highlight the most important things, transmitting the Gospel to them in a more specific way.

139During the development of the mission, it is a custom of great profit to have the “Rosary of the Dawn," which is carried out early in the morning, in which people songs and “saetas” are inserted between the mysteries; also, the path taken each day can be varied with great profit.

140The “saeta” is a little sententious and moral verse that is used in the missionary sermons, or in any other act of devotion, and the mission is the suitable moment to use it, both in the sermons and in the processions. As the true “saetas” are high pitched, swift and of long flight, they differ from the ejaculatory prayers in that the latter go from man to God, on the contrary the former go from God to man through the missionary; they contain eternal truths about: divine mercy, justice, the final judgment, sin, man's end, etc, and they have their origin in Sacred Scripture.44 The Holy Fathers also used them (Saint Jerome, Saint Cyril, Saint John Chrysostom, etc). They are not songs; they are not a hymns... The saeta wounds to kill. It should be sonorous, harmonic, it should not be affected. Although it has verse and meter, it does not try to be poetry. Many people, for the pleasant sound of the “saeta,” have passed from the sensible to the spiritual plane of the will. The missionaries of old used it with much profit.45 It is what is now, in a secular way, the " jingle." 46

c) The Missionary Act

141It is convenient to have the central act at an appropriate hour; not with the Mass if possible, it should not be together with the Mass because the Mission is fundamentally the preaching of the Word of God, and thanks to it, people will draw close to the sacraments. The structure of the missionary act generally consists in ten acts:

The procession;

A point of catechism;

The controversy;

The most important : the missionary Sermon;

The offering of flowers to the Virgin;

The Collective Prayer;

Communion;

Announcements about the Mission;

The Final blessing;

10. The Farewell and cultural act.

1421st The Procession: by which external testimony of the interior faith is given; in order that those who do not participate because of laziness or shame are attracted, by praying the Rosary and singing songs after each mystery, by carrying the images of saints to whom the people of the mission site have more devotion, and also others. We begin carrying the principle image, and then the others are collected that children, teens, women, men, etc., carry. Children usually make the procession of candles. We make a procession each day of the Mission, for 30 minutes, walking about 800 meters. At arriving to the Church, the children go to an appropriate place for the Children’s Mission.

1432nd The Point of Catechism: We usually call it the “doctrinal cartridge” to show that it should impress the audience. It is a brief (about 5 minutes) and clear exhibition of some point of Catholic doctrine. It is directed to the intelligence and should be more formative than persuasive. Its net purpose is catechetical. The topics should be those that the people need most.

1443rd The Controversy: it is a discussion in which one defends the Catholic doctrine and another attacks it using the more common arguments which people use in order not to go to Church. The attacker should be the interpreter of the people; they should identify with him, so that when the attacker is refuted, the audience is being refuted. The purpose is not to destroy the attacker, but to correct with charity. It lasts about 10 or 15 minutes.

145-It could be convenient to dramatize47 the discussion. The topics should be those that catch people’s attention most, by their present interest, by being topics which people are most ignorant about or are most questioning, these can be: the meaning of suffering, the problem of alcoholism, drugs, priestly celibacy, the reasons why bad things happen to good people and good things happen to bad people, superstitions, confession, the richness of the Vatican, priestly salary, those that sustain the most virulent sects in the area, bad in the Church, consumerism, hedonism, permissiveness, “ethical night,” divorce, abortion, bioethics, etc.

1464th-The missionary sermon: or of the end, or of shock, is the most important part of the missionary act because it is the moment in which people’s will should be moved to the practice of the virtues. It should last 30 minutes or more. Those who say that it should be shorter are those who are bad preachers, who improvise and who are not capable of developing a topic with interest, who are not convinced of the truth and of the effectiveness of Christian preaching. They bored even though they preach only a minute, and the feeling they leave is that they spoke too much. Yes, too many empty words. For this issue they should use the Directory of Preaching.

1475th- Flowers to the Virgin: at the end of the missionary Sermon, homage should be paid to the Virgin, for which it is convenient that children enter in procession carrying flowers which they place before the image. It is a very touching moment and does much good.

1486th -Then the collect prayer is made, which can be a novena, or from the title [or patron] of the parish or chapel, or any other appropriate prayer. In some places a collection for charity is made (it is convenient that many people pass the basket around).

1497th - Communion is distributed according to the corresponding Ritual.

1508th - The announcements of the Mission are clearly given, especially those for the following day, reiterating the most important from previous days.

1519th - The final blessing is given.

15210th- The faithful of the Church are dismissed, inviting those who would like to, to participate in a reception or show in the atrium or another appropriate place, with folk songs, videos of the Holy Rosary, or videos of debates, etc. The participation of the people is great and with this, the esteem and appreciation for the missionaries increase

Article 3: The Post - Mission

153- The Mission does not finish with the departure of the missionaries, on the contrary, it should be the beginning of a better Christian life or of conversion. For that reason, the permanent formation of the people should continue through the organization of different groups, confession, spiritual direction, attention to the sick, catechesis, courses about Catholic culture, spiritual exercises, conferences, monthly retreats, the use of media to defend the Gospel, parish associations, confraternities, nocturnal adoration, holy hours, Sunday schools, meditation and prayer in community, epistolary apostolate, etc.

154The " tornate " 48 is a brief mission of one, two or three days which is made after two or more months, to revive the fire kindled in the Holy Mission.

May God grant us many and holy preachers, true “authentic apostles," “burning," 49 who will spend and be utterly spent for your sakes. (2 Cor 12:15).
